```{r}
#| label: load-packages

library(leaps)
library(HH)
rents <- read.csv("rents.csv")
```

## (Temporary Section) Exploring models for predicting the monthly rent of a property.

So far the two models I have here have major issues with the conditions for multi-regressional models.

### Model 1

```{r}
rents$King <- as.numeric(rents$county == "King")
rents$Snohomish <- as.numeric(rents$county == "Snohomish")
rents$Kitsap <- as.numeric(rents$county == "Kitsap")
rents$Pierce <- as.numeric(rents$county == "Pierce")

rents$house <- as.numeric(rents$type == "house")
rents$apartment <- as.numeric(rents$type == "apartment")
rents$townhome <- as.numeric(rents$type == "townhome")

# I had to remove county and type since they are categorical and I just created numeric binary values for them
m.all <- lm(rent ~ . - county - type, data = rents)

summary(m.all)

MSE = (summary(m.all)$sigma)^2
step(m.all, scale = MSE, direction = "both")
cat("\n\nThe new Model: \n")

# I removed smoking_allowed from the model that was provided from the step function because it isn't significant with the other variable also in the model
Model <- lm(formula = rent ~ sqfeet + beds + baths + cats_allowed + dogs_allowed + electric_vehicle_charge + furnished + wd_in_unit + garage + in_seattle + in_bellevue + seattle_dist + King + 
    Snohomish + Kitsap + apartment, data = rents)

summary(Model)

plot(Model)
hist(resid(Model), n = 60)
```

### Model 2

```{r}
all <- regsubsets(rent ~ . - county - type, data = rents)
# the models are the same for both r^2 and Cp from this selection so I only showed the one plot
plot(all, scale="adjr2")
#plot(all, scale="Cp")

Model2 <- lm(rent ~ sqfeet + baths + electric_vehicle_charge + 
    furnished + wd_in_unit + in_seattle + in_bellevue + seattle_dist + Pierce, data = rents)

plot(Model2)
hist(resid(Model2), n = 60)

summary(Model2)
```
